title_en: Fan Maosheng et al. v. Huai'an Telecom Branch, Huaiyin District Telecom Bureau, and Huai'an City Huaiyin District Highway Management Station — dispute over compensation for personal injury
ruling_gist_en: The owner or manager shall timely and proactively monitor the changes in the condition of the property owned or managed by it and its impact on the rights of others, and shall bear civil tort liability for the consequences of damage caused to others due to violation of the duty of management and care, unless it can prove that it is not at fault for the occurrence of the damage.

full_text_en:
Fan Maosheng et al. v. Huai'an Telecom Branch, Huaiyin District Telecom Bureau, Yuanji Township Telecom Sub-bureau, and Huaiyin District Highway Management Station of Huai'an City — dispute over compensation for personal injury

Ruling Summary

The owner or manager shall timely and proactively monitor the changing conditions of the property under its ownership or management and their impact on the rights of others, and shall bear civil tort liability for consequences caused by personal injury due to a breach of the duty of management and care, unless it can prove that it was not at fault for the occurrence of the injury.

Plaintiffs: Fan Maosheng, male, 59 years old, Han Chinese, farmer, residing at Nongke Village, Yuanji Township, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: Ji Meihua, female, 58 years old, Han Chinese, farmer, residing at Nongke Village, Yuanji Township, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: He Sugai, female, 26 years old, Han Chinese, farmer, residing at Nongke Village, Yuanji Township, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: Fan Xuanqi, male, 1 year old, Han Chinese, residing at Nongke Village, Yuanji Township, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Defendant: Yuanji Township Telecom Sub-bureau, Huaiyin District Telecom Bureau, Huai'an Telecom Branch, domiciled at Yuanji Township, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Defendant: Huaiyin District Telecom Bureau, Huai'an Telecom Branch, domiciled at West Changjiang Road, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Zhu Ninghua, Director of the Bureau.
Defendant: Huaiyin District Highway Management Station of Huai'an City, domiciled at West Changjiang Road, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Baochun, Station Chief.

The plaintiffs, Fan Maosheng, Ji Meihua, He Sugai, and Fan Xuanqi, initiated an action with the Huaiyin District People's Court of Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants, Yuanji Township Telecom Sub-bureau, Huaiyin District Telecom Bureau, Huai'an Telecom Branch (hereinafter referred to as Yuanji Township Telecom Sub-bureau), Huaiyin District Telecom Bureau, Huai'an Telecom Branch (hereinafter referred to as the Telecom Bureau), and Huaiyin District Highway Management Station of Huai'an City (hereinafter referred to as the Highway Station), concerning a dispute over compensation for personal injury.

The four plaintiffs alleged: The plaintiffs Fan Maosheng and Ji Meihua were the parents of the deceased Fan Yujin, the plaintiff He Sugai was the wife of the deceased Fan Yujin, and the plaintiff Fan Xuanqi was the son of the deceased Fan Yujin. On December 16, 2007, Fan Yujin drove a two-wheeled motorcycle bearing license plate Su H73717 from east to west along Linjiang Road and, at approximately 2KM + 500M of Linjiang Road, collided with a utility pole located in the road, causing Fan Yujin's death. The primary responsibility for Fan Yujin's death lay with the defendants Telecom Bureau and Highway Station. Therefore, the plaintiffs requested that the two defendants compensate for: Fan Xuanqi's living expenses of RMB 41,520.60, living expenses for the fetus of RMB 43,128, death compensation of RMB 327,560, moral damages of RMB 50,000, and funeral expenses of RMB 11,874, totaling RMB 474,092.60, of which 70% was claimed, i.e., RMB 331,864.80.

The defendant Telecom Bureau argued: Fan Yujin did not die from colliding with a utility pole but from drunk driving. The utility pole allegedly struck was installed by the roadside according to standards 15 years ago. After road widening in 2004, the pole was relatively displaced within the roadbed. The Telecom Bureau did not receive any notice requiring the pole to be moved. If the relevant department had promptly notified the Telecom Bureau, the Telecom Bureau would have made corrections in accordance with such notice. Fan Yujin should bear full responsibility for this accident. The Telecom Bureau has no liability, and the plaintiffs' claims against the Telecom Bureau should be dismissed.

The defendant Highway Station argued: (1) The owner of the utility pole was the defendant Telecom Bureau, and the Highway Station should not be a defendant. In 2004, the Huaiyin District government widened and improved the road, expanding the original 7-meter-wide road surface to 9 meters. (2) The utility pole was installed over 10 years ago, and poles historically erected are not within the Highway Station's management scope. The Highway Station has no defect in road management. Moreover, the Highway Law of the PRC came into effect on January 1, 1998, so the management of the utility pole in question does not apply to the provisions of the Highway Law. (3) This accident was caused by Fan Yujin driving after drinking alcohol, and Fan Yujin should bear full responsibility. The court should dismiss the plaintiffs' claims against the Highway Station.

The Huaiyin District People's Court of Huai'an City found the following facts at first instance:

In March 2004, the Huaiyin District Committee of the CPC issued Document No. 103 (2004), requiring the widening of roads within the entire district. The road surface of county roads should be no less than 9 meters wide, and the roadbed no less than 12 meters wide. County roads were to be implemented by the District Transportation Bureau. The relocation of power, telecommunications, and broadcast and television poles within the widened roadbed was to be the responsibility of the power, telecommunications, and broadcast and television departments, respectively. To this end, the Huaiyin District Government also held a meeting of district heads and produced a meeting summary, in which relevant personnel from the defendant Telecom Bureau and the defendant Highway Station participated. The widening of the road surface of Linjiang Road caused the utility pole to be located on a roadbed only 35 centimeters from the road surface, with the road surface and roadbed essentially level. At approximately 8:20 p.m. on December 16, 2007, Fan Yujin, after drinking alcohol, drove the two-wheeled motorcycle bearing license plate Su H73717 from east to west along Linjiang Road. At 2KM + 500M of Linjiang Road, the vehicle entered the north side of the road and collided with a roadside utility pole, causing Fan Yujin to be injured and die after emergency medical treatment failed. After passersby reported the incident, the traffic police brigade of the Huaiyin Branch of the Huai'an Public Security Bureau arrived at the scene. On-site investigation confirmed that Fan Yujin was indeed injured by colliding with the utility pole and later died despite emergency medical treatment.

It was also found that the utility pole was owned by the defendant Telecom Bureau, and the management unit of that road section was the defendant Highway Station. The road section was a county road with a road surface width of 9 meters. During his lifetime, Fan Yujin was engaged in the construction and decoration industry, and relevant compensation expenses could be calculated based on the income standards for urban residents. In 2007, the per capita disposable income of urban residents in Jiangsu Province was RMB 16,378, and the per capita living consumption expenditure of rural residents was RMB 4,792.

The above facts were confirmed by the statements of both parties, the certificate from the traffic police brigade of the Huaiyin Branch of the Huai'an Public Security Bureau, the traffic accident scene diagram, the traffic accident liability determination, interrogation records, scene photographs, one copy of Document No. 103 (2004) of the Huaiyin District Committee, the meeting summary of the district heads' meeting (Document No. 71 (2004)), scene photographs and on-site inspection records collected by the court, cash tax payment certificates from the Huai'an Local Taxation Bureau before Fan Yujin's death, fund special receipts, unified invoices, and witness testimony.

The Huaiyin District People's Court of Huai'an City held at first instance:

In accordance with relevant regulations, it is prohibited to install utility poles or other facilities that obstruct traffic within the road and road land use area. Utility poles that become relatively displaced onto the road surface after road widening due to social development must be relocated promptly. The defendant Telecom Bureau, as the owner of the utility pole in question, knew or should have known that the pole was located within the road land use area and posed a safety hazard. It should have relocated it promptly but failed to do so, and therefore must bear corresponding compensation liability for breach of the duty of management and care. Regarding the Telecom Bureau's argument that the pole was installed according to standards 15 years ago and that after road widening caused relative displacement, it received no notice to move the pole, and that it had already managed and maintained the pole in accordance with the law, the court held: Widening roads serves social development and the interests of the people. While road management and other departments should indeed give notice for the sake of road smoothness, in this case, the Telecom Bureau was already aware of the situation. Even if it was not aware, it cannot thereby evade liability, because the owner and manager of property must and should pay attention to and be aware of the relative changes in the condition of the property under its ownership or management and their impact on the rights of others, and must bear compensation liability for injuries caused by defects in maintenance and management. Whether and how it followed departmental laws, regulations, and rules in managing and maintaining the pole does not constitute a valid defense against external right holders. Therefore, this defense was not accepted. The Telecom Bureau's other defenses were negated by the facts and were also not accepted. Although the defendant Highway Station, as the management unit of the road section in question, bears the responsibility of managing and protecting the smoothness of the road, the Highway Station has no authority to manage the Telecom Bureau, and their respective management norms often conflict. Under such circumstances, both defendants, particularly the Telecom Bureau as the pole owner, must in any case take the effective protection of citizens' rights as the primary consideration to actively resolve the conflict of rights. Moreover, in 2004, the Huaiyin District Committee and District Government held a meeting on road construction to determine the widening of the road and clarify respective responsibilities. The Telecom Bureau was aware of this but neglected its duty to act. Therefore, for the liability for damages caused by its failure to promptly relocate the pole, even if the Highway Station did not give further notice, it may no longer bear liability. Fan Yujin drove after drinking alcohol, directly causing the injury in this case, and must bear primary responsibility. Among the losses claimed by the four plaintiffs due to Fan Yujin's death, Fan Xuanqi's living expenses of RMB 41,520.60, death compensation of RMB 281,680, and funeral expenses of RMB 11,874, totaling RMB 380,954.60, are in accordance with the law and should be recognized. However, the Telecom Bureau should compensate an appropriate amount based on the principle of fault liability. Since the fetus in plaintiff He Sugai's womb has not yet been born, its living expenses have also not yet arisen. This claim is not supported for now and may be pursued separately after the child is born.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 106, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Article 56, Paragraph 1 and Article 70 of the Highway Law of the PRC, Article 2, Paragraph 1, Article 11, Paragraphs 1 and 2, Article 17, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases on Compensation for Personal Injury, and Article 9, Item (2) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Liability for Mental Distress in Civil Tort, on June 20, 2008, the court rendered judgment:

The losses of the plaintiffs Fan Maosheng, Ji Meihua, He Sugai, and Fan Xuanqi in the amount of RMB 380,954.60 shall be compensated by the defendant Telecom Bureau at 40%, i.e., RMB 152,881.84, and the Telecom Bureau shall also pay moral damages of RMB 10,000, totaling RMB 162,881.84, to be paid within ten days after the judgment takes effect; the other claims of the four plaintiffs are dismissed.

Both the four plaintiffs and the defendant Telecom Bureau appealed the first-instance judgment to the Huai'an Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

The four plaintiffs argued: The facts found at first instance were clear, but the judgment ordering the appellant Telecom Bureau to bear 40% of the compensation liability and pay RMB 10,000 in moral damages was too low. They requested that the second instance modify the judgment to order the Telecom Bureau to bear 50% of the compensation liability and pay RMB 40,000 in moral damages. Additionally, the respondent Highway Station neglected its duty and should also bear compensation liability.

The appellant Telecom Bureau argued: The evidence supporting the first-instance judgment that the Telecom Bureau bore liability was insufficient, and the findings of fact were erroneous. This case was a traffic accident. According to the determination of the traffic police department, the victim drove after drinking and died, which had no causal relationship with the position of the utility pole. The documents of the Huaiyin District Committee and District Government contradicted telecommunications laws and regulations and could not serve as the basis for determining facts. The victim was a farmer who only did odd jobs during the off-season, with no work unit or professional qualification certificate. The first instance's calculation of compensation based on urban resident standards had no factual or legal basis. The first instance applied the law incorrectly. Therefore, the appellant requested that the second instance quash the original judgment and modify it to find that the appellant bore no compensation liability.

The respondent Highway Station argued: The first-instance judgment was correct and should be affirmed.

The Huai'an Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Huai'an Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at second instance:

In this case, the relative of the appellants Fan Maosheng, Ji Meihua, He Sugai, and Fan Xuanqi, Fan Yujin, drove his vehicle at night after drinking alcohol, entered the north side of the road, collided with a roadside utility pole, and died after emergency medical treatment failed. Fan Yujin failed to travel under the principle of ensuring safety, which was the direct and primary cause of this accident, and he must bear primary responsibility for the injury. According to relevant regulations, it is prohibited to install utility poles and similar facilities within the road and road land use area. The appellant Telecom Bureau, as the owner of the utility pole in question, at the meeting on road construction convened by the District Committee and District Government, was assigned the responsibility to relocate the power, telecommunications, and broadcast and television poles within the 12-meter roadbed, with each department responsible for its own. This allocation of responsibility conforms to the principle of "whoever owns, manages, benefits, and is responsible," and is consistent with the legal principles of consistency of rights and obligations and fairness. Therefore, regardless of whether it conflicts with its management norms, it can serve as the factual basis for determining this case. Moreover, after the road was opened to traffic, the Telecom Bureau knew that the utility pole in question was located within the road land use area and should have relocated it promptly but failed to do so, creating a safety hazard endangering the people's interests. This undoubtedly was also a cause of Fan Yujin's death, and it should bear corresponding civil compensation liability. The first instance, based on the facts of the case, combined with the degree of fault and the causal force, determined the civil liability of both parties, which was not improper. At first instance, the four appellants submitted one cash tax payment certificate from the Huai'an Local Taxation Bureau before Fan Yujin's death, one fund special receipt, one unified invoice, and called two witnesses to testify, aiming to prove that Fan Yujin was engaged in the construction and decoration industry during his lifetime and derived his main income from urban areas. Although the Telecom Bureau objected to this evidence, it did not provide evidence to refute it. Therefore, the first instance's support for the four appellants' claim to calculate relevant compensation expenses based on urban resident standards does not violate the spirit of the law. Since the four appellants' relative, the deceased Fan Yujin, should bear primary civil liability in this case, the first instance's discretionary award of RMB 10,000 in moral damages against the Telecom Bureau is also in accordance with the law. The appellants' claim that the respondent Highway Station should bear compensation liability for the damages in this case has no factual or legal basis.

In summary, none of the appellants' grounds for appeal could be sustained. The first-instance judgment was correct and should be affirmed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, on September 8, 2008, the Huai'an Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered judgment:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
